scope: Accepted full-660 expansion of source-person coverage in the real-human versus H3 robot flower-arranging comparison
summary: v78 deliberately expands the light shadow over the complete lower-person and arm workspace, suppresses garment color and intermittent human residuals, preserves robot/flower/vegetation content, passes all 11 acceptance gates, and publishes a new 27.5-second comparison showcase.
evidence: All 11 renderer gates pass: both videos decode 660 frames; edit scope, clean-plate reduction, chroma suppression, protected content, outside safety, generated-green inheritance, full-frame jerk, ROI jerk, and human review all pass.

The lower-person semantic layer uses ROI (350,165,780,475), 48-pixel spatial dilation, +/-2-frame temporal union, 18-pixel feather, 0.88 light-graphite strength, 10-pixel robot/flower protection, and 3-pixel generated-green protection.
Mean wide-person active fraction is 0.0840429, total mean modified fraction is 0.1155060, and maximum modified fraction is 0.1477589; v74's prior total mean modified fraction was 0.0541051.
Wide-region mean chroma falls 40.67%, from 13.2482 to 7.8594, while the independent clean-plate layer reduces its mean distance by 16.9760%.
Protected robot/flower pixels, pixels outside the union safety region, and generated-green pixels relative to the inherited plate result are exact on every preencode frame.
Full-frame mean jerk is 0.773972 versus 0.697530 in raw H3, and ROI mean jerk is 1.758543 versus 1.585339; both stay inside their declared 1.12 and 1.18 bounds.

Visual review covers the full timeline at 1 FPS, every 12th lower-workarea frame, every frame in 110--136, 235--255, 384--405, and 475--492, and the 24 highest-motion review indices inherited from the motion-lag skill assessment.
The v77 prepromotion and v78 accepted robot videos are byte-identical with SHA-256 b9201ae32206f48f5aa0a83cd3b8d3b13a8f7e06cb7a4ea190488a494da376ff.

The accepted comparison and published showcase share SHA-256 fb700bfa15cb9662d7bd436392236b510e1bc6cffffcc0e0df77689e2332de5d; ffprobe reports H.264, 672x768, 24 FPS, 660 decoded frames, and 27.500 seconds.
Twenty-six focused unit tests pass; Ruff, py_compile, full video decode, and experience-ledger validation pass.
lessons: Colored garment residuals require an independent semantic source-person layer; enlarging a neutral-chroma halo alone cannot guarantee clothing containment.
A broad light material should primarily suppress chroma while retaining local luminance, otherwise the fix becomes a dark duplicate silhouette.
Generated-content protection must include green vegetation because source-person masks can overlap plants that incomplete flower instance masks do not cover.
Layer-specific metrics must measure the relevant intermediate result before later compositing layers are applied.

The lighten-shadow skill's alpha/protection discipline remains useful when the user explicitly overrides its unchanged-support default, and motion-lag high-motion frames are useful acceptance probes even when motion warping is not adopted.
limitations: WORKING is scoped to this pinned 660-frame, camera-frame 2-D H3 composite and its pinned masks; it is not a general segmentation or physical relighting claim.
The deliberately broad soft shadow can remain visible as a stylized light graphite region, as requested, though it no longer exposes recognizable garment/hand pixels in reviewed frames.
The result does not demonstrate physical robot execution.
